title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 198 (Knowledge requisite for valid ratification)

content.overview: Section 198 provides that no valid ratification can be made by a person whose knowledge of the facts of the case is materially defective.
content.glance: No valid ratification can be made by a person whose knowledge of the facts of the case is materially defective.
content.study: Section 198 provides that no valid ratification can be made by a person whose knowledge of the facts of the case is materially defective. This is the statutory rule under Section 198 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872. Apply the elements stated in the text; do not extend beyond the provision. sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: No valid ratification can be made by a person whose knowledge of the facts of the case is materially defective.

examples.title: Materially defective knowledge
examples.body: A person whose knowledge of the material facts is defective cannot validly ratify under Section 198.

hypotheticals.question: A person ratifies without material knowledge of the facts. Is the ratification valid?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 198 provides that no valid ratification can be made by a person whose knowledge of the facts of the case is materially defective.

essentialIngredients: Knowledge of the facts of the case must not be materially defective
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 198 provides that no valid ratification can be made by a person whose knowledge of the facts of the case is materially defective. Material knowledge is a prerequisite to valid ratification under Section 196.
examples: Ratification with materially incomplete knowledge of the facts is invalid.
distinctions: Knowledge requirement complements the form of ratification under Section 197.
problemApplication: Identify the state of knowledge at the time of purported ratification.
Conclude validity or invalidity under Section 198.
keyTakeaways: No valid ratification if knowledge of the facts is materially defective.

distinctions.title: Scope of Section 198
distinctions.body: Section 198 applies only to the circumstances described in its statutory text. It does not create additional grounds or remedies beyond those stated.

misconceptions.myth: Section 198 creates unlimited or extra-statutory rights.
misconceptions.correction: Section 198 operates only within the elements and consequences stated in its statutory text.
